title: Why 70% of Beginners Fail at VLSI Projects (And How to Avoid It)
short_hook: Stop buying parts you can't use.
description:
Choosing the right electronics project isn't about having the best kit—it's about avoiding the trap that stops 70% of first-year students. If you've ever bought a sensor or motor only to realize you don't know how to power it, this roadmap is for you. By the end of this video, you will have a clear, step-by-step path to pick a project that matches your actual skill level.

In this video:
- How to honestly assess if you are a Level 1, 2, or 3 student
- The Minimum Viable Project: making an LED blink
- How to orient LEDs: Anode and Cathode
- Choosing the right platform: Arduino vs. ESP32
- The 3 most common errors and how to fix them

Which of the three common errors listed—wrong LED orientation, missing resistor, or loose wire—have you encountered most in your own projects? Let me know by typing Orientation, Resistor, or Wire in the comments.
